metadata.title: Repo Research - Sources
metadata.description: Curated registry for scanning public GitHub repos across three modes: skill (agent-skill ecosystem), practice (real-team git/PR/CI), code (framework idioms). Includes high-signal authors, awesome-list entry points, per-mode target lists, and license compatibility.

registries.purpose: Open format spec for SKILL.md, frontmatter schema, directory structure

license_compatibility.Apache-2.0: permits derived work with attribution and patent grant
license_compatibility.GPL-2.0: viral copyleft — derivatives must be GPL — DO NOT USE
license_compatibility.GPL-3.0: viral copyleft — derivatives must be GPL — DO NOT USE
license_compatibility.AGPL-3.0: stronger viral copyleft — DO NOT USE
license_compatibility.CC-BY-SA-4.0: copyleft share-alike — avoid for catalog merges
license_compatibility.Proprietary: DO NOT EXTRACT — get permission first

ecosystem_analytics.name: GH Archive
ecosystem_analytics.purpose: Full GitHub event stream (WatchEvent, PushEvent, IssuesEvent, etc.) archived hourly. Use for star-spike detection and activity correlation. BigQuery dataset: bigquery-public-data.github_archive_day
ecosystem_analytics.rate_limit: No API rate limit — data downloaded as gzip hourly files or queried via BigQuery
ecosystem_analytics.example_use: SELECT DATE(created_at), COUNT(*) FROM bigquery-public-data.github_archive_day.events_* WHERE type='WatchEvent' AND repo.name='owner/repo' GROUP BY 1 — a 2000-star day with no PushEvents is almost always a fake-star burst

ecosystem_analytics.name: OSS Insight
ecosystem_analytics.purpose: Aggregated GitHub analytics: star history, contributor timelines, language trends, comparative repo analysis. REST API at api.ossinsight.io/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/. No auth required for public data.
ecosystem_analytics.rate_limit: No documented hard limit for public queries; use sparingly (pause between calls)
ecosystem_analytics.example_use: GET https://api.ossinsight.io/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/stars/history — returns daily star deltas for spike detection without BigQuery

ecosystem_analytics.name: deps.dev (Google Open Source Insights)
ecosystem_analytics.purpose: Reverse dependency counts, vulnerability advisories, and license propagation for packages across npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, Cargo. Use when assessing whether a repo is a critical shared dependency or isolated experiment.
ecosystem_analytics.rate_limit: No auth required; no documented limit for single queries
ecosystem_analytics.example_use: GET https://api.deps.dev/v3alpha/systems/npm/packages/%40vercel%2Fai — returns dependentCount, advisories, licenses for the Vercel AI SDK

ecosystem_analytics.name: Libraries.io
ecosystem_analytics.purpose: SourceRank score (composite quality signal), dependent repository count, version history, and maintainer metadata across 6M+ packages. Open dataset available for bulk analysis.

ecosystem_analytics.name: star-history.com
ecosystem_analytics.purpose: Visual star timeline for GitHub repos. An S-curve is organic growth; a vertical cliff is a purchased-star event. Use as a quick sanity check before running GH Archive queries.
ecosystem_analytics.rate_limit: Browser tool; no public API — use ossinsight.io for programmatic access
ecosystem_analytics.example_use: https://star-history.com/#owner/repo — view star growth curve to spot purchase events

cross_host_registries.name: Sourcegraph Public Search
cross_host_registries.purpose: Cross-host code search across GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket public repos. Query language: repo:, file:, content:, lang:, patternType:regexp. No auth required for public repos. Useful for finding code patterns that span multiple hosting platforms.
cross_host_registries.rate_limit: No documented public limit; throttles on very broad queries
cross_host_registries.example_use: repo:/SKILL.md$/ file:references/ lang:Markdown content:"discovery-protocol" — finds all repos with a discovery-protocol reference in a SKILL.md-rooted references dir

cross_host_registries.name: GitLab API — top repos by stars
cross_host_registries.purpose: GitLab hosts a distinct CI-template ecosystem (GitLab CI .yml templates, Auto DevOps). Use when researching CI/CD practices beyond GitHub Actions, or when a target is GitLab-native.
cross_host_registries.example_use: GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects?order_by=stars&sort=desc&per_page=20&topic=devops — top DevOps repos on GitLab for Mode B practice scan

cross_host_registries.name: Codeberg / SourceHut (note)
cross_host_registries.purpose: Niche systems-tooling and privacy-focused communities. Codeberg (Gitea-based) and SourceHut host a small but high-signal set of Rust/C/Go systems tools and minimal-dependency libraries. Worth checking when Mode C targets low-dependency systems code not well-represented on GitHub.
cross_host_registries.rate_limit: Codeberg API mirrors Gitea: 30 req/min unauthenticated. SourceHut: varies by service.

april_2026_caveats.llm_generated_spam: Since late 2025, many agent-skill repos are LLM-generated shells. Triage: commit history before 2025-09, varied file sizes, issue/PR activity, description not ending in '...for Claude/Codex'.
april_2026_caveats.topic_noise: topic:agent-skills has >5000 results, ~60% low-signal. Prefer topic:claude-skills / topic:codex-skills or named authors.
april_2026_caveats.awesome_list_drift: Many awesome-lists are LLM-curated and link to dead or LLM-generated repos. Spot-check 3 random entries before trusting.
april_2026_caveats.scorecard_gaps: OpenSSF Scorecard is widely adopted but not universal. Fall back to CODEOWNERS + commit-signing ratio + contributor count for repos without Scorecard.
